text:
**Night-shift naps and the drive home**

This article reports on a simulator study of 96 night-shift workers. The study tested whether a 20-minute nap at 3am improves driving home afterward.

- **Overall:** When workers napped, lane drifting fell by 22%, and reaction time improved by 0.09 seconds. In other words, the nap was associated with measurable gains in both measures during the simulated drive.
- **Not for everyone:** The benefits went mostly to workers with 6 or more months on nights. For new night workers, defined as those under 3 months, lane drifting did not improve. Some of these workers also felt groggy for about 15 minutes after waking, so the nap did not clearly help them.
- **Timing matters more:** Drives at 7am showed about twice the lane drifting of drives at 6am, whether or not the driver had napped. Put differently, the time of day of the drive had a larger effect on lane drifting than the nap did.

**Takeaway:** Naps can be a cheap aid for experienced staff, but they are not a substitute for earlier shift end times or for transport home after long shift runs. It is worth keeping this in mind when deciding how to support night-shift drivers as a whole.

**Caveats:** These findings come from a simulator only, not real roads. The participants were mostly men aged 25–50, so the results may not apply equally to other groups.
